length.text: Popular sources give 6-9 m; such sizes are rare

overview.text: The Green Anaconda is the heaviest snake in the world: a huge, non-venomous boa of the rivers and swamps of tropical South America. In 2024 scientists split it into two species, the Southern Green Anaconda (*Eunectes murinus*) and the Northern Green Anaconda (*E. akayima*), which look identical but differ in their DNA.

size.label: Sizes reported
size.text: National Geographic gives 6 to 9 m and up to about 227 kg, but the heaviest weights are estimates rather than careful measurements, and a researcher who measured over a thousand wild anacondas found very large ones to be rare.

distribution.label: Before the 2024 split
distribution.text: Tropical South America east of the Andes, in the Amazon and Orinoco basins.

distribution.label: After the split
distribution.text: The Southern Green Anaconda (*E. murinus*) lives in Peru, Bolivia, Brazil and French Guiana; the Northern Green Anaconda (*E. akayima*) in Ecuador, Colombia, Venezuela, Trinidad, Guyana, Suriname and French Guiana. SnakeList's map still shows the green anaconda in the older, broad sense.

behaviour.text: Usually solitary: adults keep to their own hunting areas except in the breeding season.

diet.text: A constrictor that can tackle very large animals, including caimans and even jaguars.

taxonomy.text: A 2024 study found that northern and southern green anacondas differ genetically by about 5.5% and split roughly 10 million years ago, and named the northern one *Eunectes akayima*. Because the two cannot be told apart by appearance, some experts dispute the split.

funfacts.text: Its genus name *Eunectes* means good swimmer.
